transcriptText:
Middle position raises to 25. You're on the button. When do you raise again? Only with aces or kings? Or the best hands... plus a few that block them? Make your pick.

Say you only 3-bet aces and kings. 12 combos... under 1% of hands. Easy to read. They fold everything else. So start with value. Queens or better, and ace-king. 34 combos... the hands that beat their calls. Then add pressure. Ace-five and ace-four suited. 42 in all... about 3%.

Why those two? Say you hold the ace and five of diamonds. Your ace takes aces away from them. Pocket aces drop from 6 combos to 3. Ace-king, 16 to 12. Kings stay at 6. Their strongest hands go from 22... down to 15. So you 3-bet to 75. 3× their raise, in position. They owe 50 more to call. Out of position, go 4×. A hundred.

Your turn. Queens, in the big blind. The button opens to 25. Choose first... Queens are value, and you're out of position. 3-bet to a hundred. You posted 10, so you owe 90 more. 3-bet the hands that beat their calls... and a few that block their best. 3× in position. 4× out. Up next: ranges.
